title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 3rd Congressional District
area: Central New Jersey, covering Burlington County and parts of Ocean and Mercer counties, including Willingboro, Mount Laurel, and Toms River.

context.text: Incumbent Herbert C. Conaway Jr. ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary. Michael McGuire won a three-way Republican primary with 57.9% of the vote (14,810 votes), ahead of Jason Cullen (24.4%) and Justin Barbera (17.7%).

Cook Political Report rated the district's Partisan Voter Index as D+5 as of September 2026; Kamala Harris won the district 53.4%–45.0% under the current district lines in the 2024 presidential election.

candidates.name: Herbert C. Conaway Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the June 2 Democratic primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 3rd Congressional District (since 2025); physician

summary.text: Herbert C. Conaway Jr. is a physician and attorney and a former U.S. Air Force Medical Corps officer who represented Burlington County-area District 7 in the New Jersey General Assembly from 1998 to 2024, chairing its Health Committee, before winning election to Congress in 2024. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary and is seeking a second term.

background.text: According to his House biography, he is a lifelong Burlington County resident and the son of a teacher and a nurse. He graduated from Bordentown Regional High School in 1981.
Earned a B.A. in politics from Princeton University in 1985, an M.D. from Jefferson Medical College in 1989, and a J.D. from Rutgers Law School, Camden, in 1996.

Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1992 to 1996, reaching the rank of Captain in the Medical Corps at McGuire Air Force Base, where his House biography says he worked as a general medical officer and rose to assistant director of the primary care clinic.

After an internal medicine residency, practiced in primary care settings and became a clinical professor at an inner-city community hospital, according to his House biography; Ballotpedia lists his professional experience as a private practicing physician and work at Cooper University Hospital.

Served in the New Jersey General Assembly representing District 7 from 1998 until his election to Congress in 2024, chairing the Health Committee and serving on the Budget, Appropriations, and Military and Veterans' Affairs committees.

His House biography credits him with sponsoring New Jersey's school funding formula and with legislation on public school nutrition, environmental protection, property tax relief, veterans' services, and public safety.
Won the open 3rd District seat in November 2024 with 53.2% of the vote over Republican Rajesh Mohan, succeeding Rep. Andy Kim, and took office in January 2025.

Serves in the 119th Congress on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittee on Health and Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations) and the Committee on Small Business (Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access). Advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Says restoring affordability for middle-class families is a top priority, citing his advocacy for expanding the Child Tax Credit and the state and local tax (SALT) deduction, and his support for the Shrinkflation Reduction Act of 2024.

Says protecting reproductive rights is a priority, pointing to his record co-sponsoring reproductive-privacy legislation in the Assembly and his support in Congress for codifying Roe v. Wade and the Right to Contraception Act.

Prioritizes lowering prescription drug prices, citing his work as Assembly Health Committee chair capping co-pays on insulin and other life-saving drugs and requiring more pharmaceutical-industry transparency.

positions.summary: Supports codifying Roe v. Wade into federal law and the Right to Contraception Act; as a state legislator co-sponsored a bill protecting nondisclosure of reproductive-healthcare patient information and access for out-of-state patients.

As Assembly Health Committee chair, worked to cap co-pays on insulin and other life-saving drugs and increase pharmaceutical pricing transparency; supports taking similar drug-cost caps to the national level.
Advocates expanding the Child Tax Credit and the SALT deduction to help middle-class families, rather than framing his platform around taxing wealthy individuals specifically.

In the Assembly, introduced legislation establishing a New Jersey Invasive Species Task Force and a bill providing income tax credits for zero-emission lawn equipment; supports expanding electric-vehicle charging infrastructure nationally.

record.text: Chaired the New Jersey General Assembly's Health Committee, where he led efforts to cap co-pays for 30-day supplies of life-saving drugs including epinephrine injectors, asthma inhalers, and insulin, and required pharmacies to document reasons for not filling certain prescriptions.

Sponsored the "Manufacturing in Higher Education Act" as a state legislator, promoting manufacturing career pathways for students, and supported the New Jersey Economic Recovery Act of 2020, which provided $14 billion in pandemic relief to small businesses and restaurants.

Co-sponsored New Jersey Assembly bill A3975, protecting nondisclosure of patient information related to reproductive healthcare services and protecting access to abortion-related services for out-of-state persons.
As a state legislator, sponsored bills to improve the ballot-counting process and pushed to establish a Voting Improvement Task Force.

Sits on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Health; Oversight and Investigations subcommittees) and the Committee on Small Business (Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access subcommittee) for the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

candidates.name: Michael McGuire
candidates.ballotNote: Won a three-candidate June 2 Republican primary with 57.9% of the vote

summary.text: Michael McGuire is a family law attorney, U.S. Marine Corps veteran, member of the U.S. Navy Reserve, and former New York City police officer who won the Republican nomination for NJ-3 in the June 2, 2026 primary. He has not previously held elected office. He says he is running on affordability, veterans' issues, and term limits for members of Congress.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1997 to 2001 and subsequently in the U.S. Navy Reserve, where he remains a member.
Describes his background as including service as a law enforcement officer; news reports describe him as a former New York City police officer.
Works as an attorney; the New Jersey Globe describes his practice as family law and divorce. He lives in Freehold Township, according to the same report.

Told the New Jersey Globe that he had run for school board in the past; the paper reported that his decision to run for Congress followed the fall 2025 federal government shutdown, during which he and fellow Navy reservists missed paychecks.
Launched his congressional campaign in January 2026 and defeated Jason Cullen and Justin Barbera in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 57.9% of the vote.
Endorsed by Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden, former U.S. Rep. Barry Morris Goldwater Jr., the Monmouth County Republican Committee, and the Mercer County Republican Committee.

priorities.text: Says his top priority is restoring affordability and economic security for working families, starting with cutting government spending that he says fuels inflation.
priorities.quote: New Jersey, with the highest tax burden per person, is ground zero of the affordability crisis. Working families are being squeezed from every direction—by the rising cost of housing, skyrocketing grocery bills, higher energy prices, unaffordable healthcare, and a never-ending tax burden.

priorities.text: Supports congressional term limits, arguing that elected office has become a career rather than a temporary duty assignment.
As a veteran, prioritizes military readiness and funding, and says he wants to fix VA healthcare systems including mental-health services for veterans.

positions.summary: Supports strengthening border security through enforcement of existing immigration laws.
Prioritizes lowering taxes and reducing regulation to make New Jersey more affordable, rather than raising taxes on high earners or corporations.
Frames his healthcare priority as lowering costs so families keep more of their own earnings, rather than expanding public coverage.

summary.text: Ryan Kelly is a public servant whose background, by his own account, spans public service, education, and civil rights, including work at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. He is running for NJ-3 on the "Affordability, Accountability, People Party" ballot line, with a campaign he describes as focused on affordability, accountability, and practical governance.

background.text: Attended Woodland Park High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Colorado State University in 2005 and a graduate degree from Monmouth University in 2007.
In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, says his background is in public service, education, and civil rights, including work at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

priorities.text: Says his campaign is focused on affordability, accountability, and making government work for people rather than itself.
priorities.quote: My campaign is focused on affordability, accountability, and making government work for people again—not itself.

priorities.text: Wants to restore government transparency and oversight, saying decisions should be made openly and in the public interest.

positions.summary: Says he wants to expand access to affordable housing as part of lowering the cost of living for working families.

summary.text: Steven Welzer is a longtime Green Party activist and a founding member of the Green Party of New Jersey (1997) who worked in tech support for the New Jersey Judiciary for nearly 25 years. He has been a Green Party candidate for Governor, Congress, and the General Assembly. He is running for NJ-3 on ranked-choice voting, reducing military spending, and Green New Deal-style environmental policy.

background.text: Born in Newark, New Jersey, and, by his own account, a lifelong New Jersey resident; graduated from Columbia High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Rutgers University in 1976 and a master's degree in Economics from Rutgers in 1983.

Says he worked in tech support for the New Jersey Judiciary for almost 25 years; has also worked as a journalist, co-edited the print version of Green Horizon Magazine, and serves on the editorial board of its successor webzine, New Green Horizons.

Founding member of the Green Party of New Jersey in 1997; says he served on the Steering Committee of the Green Party of the United States in 2012 and is a member of the Green Party of New Jersey's Elections Committee.

Ran as a Green Party candidate for the General Assembly in District 14 in 2009, 2011, 2015 and 2025, for Governor of New Jersey in 2013, and for U.S. House in New Jersey's 12th District in 2014 and 2016; he lost each general election.
Ran in the 2024 general election for NJ-3, receiving 0.9% of the vote in the race won by Herb Conaway.
Describes living in East Windsor with his wife, Laura, and daughter, Nicole, and working to establish an ecovillage in Kimberton, Pennsylvania.

priorities.text: Wants to open the electoral system to "more voices and more choices" through ranked-choice voting and proportional representation, along with public financing of elections.
Supports Green New Deal-style measures to curb emissions and regenerate habitat, saying ecological responsibility must be central to government and economic policy.
Wants to cut the Pentagon budget substantially and shift the United States toward diplomacy over militarism, saying overseas bases provoke rather than prevent conflict.
priorities.quote: The Pentagon budget is bloated. The United States spends more on militarism than the next six countries combined! We have over 700 bases in dozens of foreign countries. They don't make us safer; rather, they provoke conflagrations.

positions.summary: Supports a Green New Deal-style program to invest in renewable energy infrastructure, end fossil-fuel subsidies, and require new buildings to reach zero emissions by 2035.
Supports codifying Roe v. Wade and ensuring full reproductive rights and bodily autonomy.

Describes U.S. involvement in overseas conflicts as driven by a "bipartisan endless war machine" and calls for cutting the military budget in favor of diplomacy, in the context of describing constituents' concerns about relatives in Gaza.

Biographical detail for Ryan Kelly is limited to his Ballotpedia profile and survey; no campaign website or news profile was loaded.
